Best practices (industry):
Power and battery:
• Power budget with a margin of at least 20 % on each supply rail
• Reverse-polarity and overvoltage protection (diode, TVS) at every power input
• Keyed connectors, sized for the current and the number of mating cycles expected
• Lithium battery: IEC 62133-2 cells, battery management circuit (overcharge, deep discharge, short circuit, temperature), UN 38.3 transport
• Decoupling and filtering as close as possible to each integrated circuit

• Proven solution or qualified off-the-shelf part rather than a new technology, unless there is a quantified reason
• Quantified, verifiable requirement in the CdCF (Goldmine) for this function, with its tolerance

Good practices (industry):
Electronics and software:
• Watchdog and a defined safe state at startup, on fault and on loss of power
• IEC 60730-1 Annex H (Class B) if the software performs a safety function
• Coding rules (e.g. MISRA C), code review and static analysis before each release
• Automated unit and integration tests, re-run on every change
• Input validation, timeouts and automatic recovery of communications
• Non-volatile memory protected by CRC, writes limited to the memory's endurance
• Signed update with the ability to roll back to the previous version
• Sensors: filtering and debouncing, thresholds with hysteresis, plausibility check of the measurement
